recommendations: Define one versioned executable Node contract as source of truth, covering tool inputs, output JSON schema, authentication, maximum results, pagination/completeness, error/status and business coverage. Treat Java implementation as a separate optional reference until explicitly integrated.

Before further training, choose whether the intended target is current V5 four-route service or a new eight-action financial router. For eight actions, explicitly implement retrieve/redirect execution behavior and bounded capability state; do not hide them inside answer or silently map unavailable retrieval to a success.

Version parameter grounding and tool sufficiency policy: direct known-ID detail can be preferred, but alternative list queries should be judged against available fields and latest50 coverage instead of assumed Java fields.
Keep component action accuracy, tool sufficiency, deterministic grounding, auth/ownership, policy-guard decisions, rules fallback and user-facing outcome as separate evaluation columns.
Current-no-KB/handoff-unavailable must be explicit deployment capability profiles; future knowledge retrieval samples remain planned capabilities, not evidence that current service can retrieve.
Do not rewrite frozen prior experiment labels. Propose disputed training groups in a new contract-audit version for separate review; do not source new examples from held-out mistakes.
open_questions: Which new eight-action protocol/version should replace or coexist with V5?
Should missing detail tool permit list-first lookup when only status/amount is asked, and how to represent partial50 coverage?
Which machine-readable fields should cover recent tool result, completeness, failure/retry and trusted UI context?
What are the product definitions for redirect and unavailable retrieve/human behavior?
What provider is actually deployed now? Static defaults are rules; explicit startup scripts choose Jev/Qwen, but live deployment was not queried.
